lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 113, for issue 93: Enter on a file path in the location bar now selects the file.
lines.say: This is a tour of pull request one thirteen, for issue ninety-three: Enter on a file path in the location bar now selects the file.

lines.caption: It has three parts: what this PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
Enter on a file's path now goes to its folder, selects the file, scrolls to it and puts the keyboard on it.
You press Ctrl+L, type the full path to a file, and press Enter.
lines.say: You press Control L, type the full path to a file, and press Enter.

lines.caption: Thunar checks the file and mounts its location if needed, keeping hold of the window until that finishes.
Instead of launching the file, the current tab moves to the file's folder. No new window opens.
The file is selected once the folder has loaded, and scrolled into view.
Then the file view takes the keyboard, so a key like Ctrl+C acts on the file.
lines.say: Then the file view takes the keyboard, so a key like Control C acts on the file.

lines.caption: A folder path still opens the folder, and a missing path still shows the same error.
Before, Enter on a file opened it in its app, and a script could even run. Now Thunar shows the file, like Nautilus.
The location bar finds its window, and reuses the window's helper that already waits for a folder to load.
A remote path can finish after the bar's temporary entry has gone, which is why the window is held from the start.
The bar is then reset to show the folder, not the file's path.
Without the focus step, a file in the folder already shown left the keyboard in the location bar.
Only opened folders are added to Recent now. A file that was only selected is not.
In the code, the launch call is replaced by four steps: find the parent, open it, select the file, and focus the view.
It stays in the current tab, unlike Open Item Location, which opens tabs per folder.
A hidden file, with hidden files not shown, opens its folder with nothing selected. The issue accepts that.
To open the file, press Enter again once it's selected, or double-click it.
The PR changes one source file, adds one verify script, and adds this page and its narration.
To undo it, revert the PR, and Enter on a file path launches the file again.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
The building session built and tested it in a cloud container, then reviewed it. CI's run wasn't finished yet.
It follows the issue's plan, reuses the window's select helper, and copies how Nautilus behaves.
The first test run passed 15 of 17: Enter on a script in the folder already shown left the keyboard in the bar.
lines.say: The first test run passed fifteen of seventeen: Enter on a script in the folder already shown left the keyboard in the bar.

lines.caption: After the focus fix, the second run passed all 17 tests.
lines.say: After the focus fix, the second run passed all seventeen tests.

lines.caption: Each file was really selected, checked by copy and paste, and the script was selected without running.
The review fixes were only compiled, and remote paths, hidden files and Recent were not tested.
So CI's verify run on the final code is the one to trust. Its results are in the PR's comments.
A fresh review agent found eight problems. Four were fixed, one was this page, and three were left on purpose.
Fixes covered the bar's text, a stale comment, remote paths, and what goes into Recent.
Left as they are: hidden files, a folder read twice, and the old function name, kept to stay close to upstream.
CI reviews every code push too, and reports in the PR's code review comment.
Real use on the owner's desktop, and a file on a remote server, can only be checked after the merge.
The PR, the issue and the test script are all linked here.
Part 3. What comes later.
No open issue depends on this one. The batch runs it alongside issues 17 and 16, which change other files.
lines.say: No open issue depends on this one. The batch runs it alongside issues seventeen and sixteen, which change other files.

lines.caption: Bookmarks in the side pane, and rename in place, don't use the location bar.
In short: type a file's path, press Enter, and Thunar shows you the file instead of opening it.
